text:
oliver: quick sync — I ran a microbenchmark this morning that shows two weird things after the kernel affinity change: 1) batch formation time variance up ~18% for short prompts, 2) KV hit rate drops slightly during high jitter windows. sharing numbers below, need ideas on tuning coalesce/jitter + token budget.
jess: can you paste the config you used? was this on canary or mainline?

oliver: canary branch (kernel-affinity-v2), 8xA100. config excerpt:
```
micro_batch_ms: 5
coalesce_delay_us: 3500
jitter: uniform(0, 2ms)
max_tokens_per_batch: 1024
queue_policy: old_first
```

arun: that jitter distrib looks narrow — uniform can cause clustering when arrival is bursty. did you try stratified jitter?

oliver: not in this run. i also captured KV hit stats (per-second):
```
time, requests, kv_hits, kv_miss_rate
00:01, 1250, 1045, 16.4%
00:02, 1420, 1120, 21.1%  <-- spike correlates with coalesce window slip
00:03, 1100, 950, 13.6%
```

maria: 21% miss is small but can amplify token work. could be that kernel affinity change moved some fast callers to a different worker so their prefix KV wasn't warm. any trace ids?

oliver: i captured a flame sample around the spike — shows more time spent in kernel-switch overhead and a short period where the KV priming path ran (priming path = disk->mem promoted). attaching log snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T09:12:21Z] worker-7 kernel-switch start
[2026-03-17T09:12:21Z] queue: formed batch size 6 latency 7.8ms (expected 5.1ms)
[2026-03-17T09:12:21Z] kv: miss -> priming async start
[2026-03-17T09:12:21Z] kernel-load: select fp16-optim-kernel -> fallback to fp16-generic (slow path)
```

kai: fallback kernel selection there is interesting — that can increase per-token time and lengthen batch windows, which then increases the chance of KV misses for subsequent requests. Did the kernel size/seq-length heuristic change in affinity-v2?

oliver: small tweak: we now prefer specialized tiled kernels for seq<=64 on certain SMs. probably misrouted some 8-32 token calls to a node without that kernel loaded.

jess: two levers we should try in tandem: 1) make jitter stratified with micro-shards to avoid phase alignment, 2) reduce coalesce_delay by a small delta and increase token_budget to keep throughput stable. suggestion example:
```
jitter: stratified(buckets=8, range=0.5ms-3ms)
coalesce_delay_us: 2500
token_budget: adaptive(target_tokens=900, floor=128, ceiling=2048)
```

arun: sgtm. also switch queue_policy to prioritize hot callers (hot_first) for a short canary, to see if KV hit rate stabilizes. if hot callers consistently get primed, cache hit improves.

maria: small experiment plan:
- canary A: stratified jitter + token_budget up + old_first queue (30m)
- canary B: stratified jitter + token_budget up + hot_first queue (30m)
- measure: batch formation variance, p50/p95 latency, kv_miss_rate, kernel-fallback-rate

oliver: running canary A now. perf-bot will post metrics when ready.

perf-bot: [automated] canary A started at 2026-03-17T09:42:00Z on canary-nodeset-3 :rocket:

arun: one more idea — add a tiny randomized clockwalk offset per worker that slowly rotates (phase shift) to avoid long-term alignment. implementation: each worker picks offset ~Uniform(-0.5ms, +0.5ms) every 5s. very low overhead.

jess: yes, clockwalk + stratified jitter reduces synchronized microbursts. but be careful: too much offset can raise p50. keep amplitude small.

oliver: results after 30m canary A (summary):
- batch formation variance down 9%
- p50 latency -2.1% p95 -1.8%
- kv_miss_rate overall -2.6pp (from 17.9% -> 15.3%)
- kernel-fallback-rate unchanged (~0.8%)

maria: decent. not fully solved but trending right. can we get a sample trace of the periods that still trigger fallback?

oliver: attached sample trace id trace-cc-172: shows kernel-check ordering still picks fallback when batch includes mixed seq_lengths (8 + 128). my thought: add a fast-path check in batch formation that splits mixed-seq batches when that reduces fallback probability and overall latency.

arun: splitting mixed batches is good but increases scheduling overhead. consider heuristics: if expected kernel penalty > X ms, split; else keep coalesced. we can estimate penalty from per-kernel perf table.

jess: propose a lightweight scoring function:
score = estimated_extra_token_ms * expected_tokens_in_batch - cost_split_overhead_ms
if score > 0 -> split.

kai: sounds good. also monitor effect on throughput; splitting could reduce amortized kernel load. we should gate this with an A/B toggle in runtime.

oliver: action items:
- arun: add stratified jitter + clockwalk offset + token_budget adaptive on canary B (hot_first)
- jess: implement split heuristic prototype in batcher (feature-flagged)
- maria: define metrics/dashboard for kernel-fallback-rate and split benefit

maria: timeline?

oliver: arun start now, jess can push prototype by EOD, i'll run a 2h canary after that. thanks all. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: [automated] canary A metrics posted -> link: https://perf.redwood.internal/canary/2334567890

jess: lgtm. if canary B reduces fallback_rate and keeps p95 stable we can roll to 20% traffic tomorrow.

arun: starting canary B with hot_first queue and clockwalk offsets. will report in ~2h.

oliver: noted. closing this thread for now, will reopen if regressions show up.
